thread:
Ava (Support): Customer AcmeCorp hitting repeated function/tool-call failures in prod. They send large binary args (base64 attachments) and see a vague 400 + truncated payload behavior. Request id r-0a1b2c3d. Reported ~2026-03-16T18:02Z.

Jamal (SRE): Can you paste the raw client request header + partial body and the exact error the API returned? Is customer blocked or has a workaround?

Ava (Support): They're blocked for some flows. Customer provided this minimal repro (sanitized):

```http
POST /v1/functions/invoke HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 245678

{
  "tool": "file-processor",
  "args": { "file_b64": "<very long base64 blob>" }
}
```

Response: 400 {"error":"payload_truncated", "message":"request body truncated by gateway"}  (from our front gateway).

Priya (ML Eng): Thanks — this screams "ingress truncation" rather than app schema. Two quick hypotheses:
1) Client used `--data` (curl) which forces buffering and a Content-Length header; some front gateways have a per-request byte limit and will drop if > limit.
2) Chunked transfer mismatch + an older router rollback earlier today.

Repro tip: try sending with `--data-binary` and/or chunked transfer to see if it bypasses buffering:

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @payload.json \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/functions/invoke
```

Also check whether their client includes a malformed `Content-Length` (too small). Can we pull the full upstream logs for r-0a1b2c3d?

Ben (Eng Oncall): I pulled the ingress logs around that timestamp. We had a gateway config bump at 2026-03-16T17:55Z to roll out a smaller default max request body for the edge cluster (temporary mitigation for a DOS vector). That change set client_max_body_size from 50MB -> 20MB. I see a cluster of 413/400 errors starting right after.

redwood-bot: Noted. Created incident INC-2026-312 with tag `ingress-body-limit`.

Ava (Support): Customer was told to try streaming in chunks or upload to our presigned S3 and pass a URL; they tried presigned URL and that flow succeeded. They prefer inline base64 for simplicity though.

Priya (ML Eng): Short-term mitigation for customer: use presigned upload or split base64 into smaller arg chunks and reassemble in the tool. Long-term: we should either restore default max body size or implement a negotiated fallback (413 with clear metadata + guidance).

Jamal (SRE): I'll roll back the temporary limit for the affected edge pool; rollback ETA ~15m. Also adding a metric alert for sudden spikes in `gateway.413.count` with customer-scoped attribution.

Sam (AcmeCS): Thanks, Ava/Jamal. We switched to presigned uploads and those requests passed. Will follow up if any remaining failures. Appreciated the quick turnaround. :relieved:

Priya (ML Eng): Follow-up items:
- Create a small reproduction test that sends 100MB base64 payloads with both `--data` and `--data-binary` (PR #742).
- Update gateway config to return a stable, explicit error schema for truncated payloads: `{"error":"payload_truncated", "limit": <bytes>, "received": <bytes>}`.
- Consider offering a server-side streaming API for function args (to avoid full-buffer semantics).

Ben (Eng Oncall): Rollback complete at 2026-03-16T18:16Z. Errors dropped to baseline. I opened ENG-789 to track the gateway error schema change and ENG-790 for streaming API evaluation.

Ava (Support): Marking this thread resolved for the customer. Customer asked for a permanent fix — I'm escalating ENG-789 with high priority. Closing note: SR# SR-2026-1145, affected customer AcmeCorp, workaround: presigned upload or chunked args.

Sam (AcmeCS): Confirmed our last two big-file calls succeeded after switching. We appreciate the root cause explanation.

Ava (Support): Great — will follow up once ENG-789 lands. :thumbsup:
